claim_text: Orchestra was hit by a cyberattack, the company's president says
summary: The company's president told two trade outlets that Orchestra is the victim of a cyberattack, with 'illicit access' found overnight Nov 19 to 20. On Nov 23 Le Figaro, a national daily, also reported the intrusion.
detail: L'Echo touristique and TourMaG each quote him. L'Echo touristique's publisher is a Travelsoft subsidiary, so TourMaG and Le Figaro are the independent checks. Travelsoft has not published a notice on its own site, as far as we found.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The company's president is quoted by three outlets, two of them independent of Travelsoft.

claim_text: The company shut down all its systems as a precaution
summary: The company's president says it switched off all its systems after seeing abnormal activity, to protect them and prevent data theft and hacking.
detail: He says the main risk was that codes could be used to make illicit bookings of trips and plane tickets. He told Le Figaro the company 'preventively unplugged and put on standby' its platforms.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Three outlets quote the company's president on the shutdown.

claim_text: Booking sites of Voyages E.Leclerc, Carrefour Voyages, Selectour and Havas Voyages went offline
summary: L'Echo touristique lists these four brands among the sites directly hit; TourMaG names Leclerc, Havas and Carrefour among the sites offline.
detail: The company's president says 'dozens' of business and consumer platforms were affected. Travel agents could not book through Orchestra and had to use the phone or other tour operators' sites. Le Figaro (Nov 23) also names Leclerc Voyages, Carrefour Voyages, Selectour and Havas Voyages, plus a tour operator, as disrupted between Friday and Sunday.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Three outlets, two independent of Travelsoft, report these sites disrupted.

claim_text: All customer platforms were back by Monday morning, Nov 23, the company says
summary: On Sunday evening, Nov 22, the company's president told L'Echo touristique that all customer platforms but one were working, with the last due Monday. On Monday Nov 23 he told Le Figaro that 'the last client was reconnected this morning'.
detail: Restoration began gradually at about 10 PM on Friday Nov 20; on Saturday morning B2C sites were still very disrupted. On Monday the president of one travel network that uses Orchestra told L'Echo touristique that things were almost back to normal, with a small back-office data problem that does not stop sales. Travelsoft has not published a notice, and we have not seen a statement from each affected brand. On Nov 24 TourMaG quoted an unnamed industry boss saying Carrefour was still blocked on Monday morning and two or three online agencies had not reopened; TourMaG saw only the flight search on the Carrefour Voyages home page that Monday.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The company's account, carried by L'Echo touristique and by Le Figaro (independent). It rests on the company's word; TourMaG's industry sources describe a slower restart for some customers.

claim_text: The data protection authority was notified
summary: The company's president says the bodies that must be alerted in a cyberattack, such as the French data protection authority (CNIL), have been told.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet, quoting the company. The regulator has not been heard from.

claim_text: The attackers got logins and passwords, TourMaG reports
summary: TourMaG says that, according to its information, the company asked all customers to change their passwords because the attackers had retrieved logins and passwords stored on its servers.
detail: This is TourMaG's reporting from unnamed sources. On Nov 22 the company's president told L'Echo touristique that Travelsoft asked suppliers to change their login credentials while an investigation runs, and that it changed passwords in its own systems and added security measures. He did not say that logins were stolen. On Nov 24 TourMaG reported that the company's technical teams were renewing database credentials, password-encoding keys and some partner access, and that operators were still changing passwords with travel agents at Orchestra's request.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet reports the theft from unnamed sources; the company describes password changes but does not confirm theft.

claim_text: Customer or traveler data was stolen
summary: The company's president says it cannot yet say whether there was a data leak, and that Orchestra does not hold bank card data.
detail: TourMaG says it does not know how much data was taken or what the intruders could see. No leak, ransom demand or claim of responsibility has been reported. On Nov 23 the company's president told Le Figaro that, so far, nothing points to payment data or customers' personal data, and that the investigation continues. On Nov 24 the company's president told TourMaG that few customers in its portfolio were touched and that 'no critical elements were hacked'.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: No source reports any confirmed theft; the company says nothing so far points to it and that nothing critical was hacked.

claim_text: Fraudulent bookings were made with stolen access
summary: The company's president named illicit bookings as the main risk. On Nov 22 he told L'Echo touristique: 'We have not identified any fraudulent booking.'
detail: No source reports that any were made. Le Figaro (Nov 23) says none had been announced. TourMaG warns of a possible wave of phishing aimed at travel professionals.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The sources describe a risk, and the company says it found none; no source reports one.

summary: No source says who the attackers are. No claim of responsibility or ransom demand has been reported. How they got in is reported by TourMaG (see the next claim).
detail: An earlier TourMaG article repeated unnamed claims that Orchestra had no two-step sign-in; that is not verified. The company's president says an investigation is under way: 'We are continuing our investigations' (Le Figaro, Nov 23).
label: Not established

claim_text: About 60 business customers were affected, the company says
summary: The company's president told Le Figaro that 'about sixty of our professional clients' may have been affected before a gradual restart from Friday evening.
detail: This is the first count given. No count of travelers or travel agents has been given.
label: Reported

claim_text: The intruders got in through a flaw in an old JBoss 4 application server, TourMaG reports
summary: TourMaG says, from its own information, that the intrusion came through one of Orchestra's servers via a flaw in JBoss 4, an application server not updated since 2008. A critical flaw in it was flagged in July 2017.
detail: Asked about it, the company's president told TourMaG it is 'a fairly old application server', tied to some customers or peripheral and not at the core of the platform, and that 'it should not have been left lying around'. He did not say in the quotes published that it was the way in. TourMaG also reports, without naming its sources, that the intrusion began at 11:45 PM on Thursday Nov 19 and was spotted at about 4:30 AM on Friday after about five hours of exploring and running commands. No second outlet, official notice or researcher has confirmed the method.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One independent outlet reports the method from its own sources; the company's president acknowledges the old server exists but the published quotes do not confirm it as the entry point.
